get.description:
What the connector form needs to know.

``can_add``: a signed-in person who may add connectors in the workspace
(Owner or Editor). ``allow_list_applies``: an administrator's server is a
site server and must be on the allow-list; anyone else's is their own and
only needs to be a public https address (``server_origin``).

post.description:
Test a remote MCP server before saving it and list its tools.

Signed-in sessions only (no access tokens), with permission to add
connectors in the workspace, and rate limited. The server must resolve to
public addresses, and a site server's host (an administrator's) must be on
the allow-list. Every failure gets the same generic message: the reply
never carries error text, so this cannot be used to probe what the
backend can reach.

post.description:
Hybrid semantic + keyword search over a workspace's knowledge base.

Thin REST door onto the same retriever the chat agent uses: returns the most
relevant documents with their matching passages, ranked by relevance.
Requires DOCUMENTS_READ permission for the workspace.

get.description:
Lightweight document title search optimized for mention picker (@mentions).

Returns only id, title, and document_type - no content or metadata.
Uses pg_trgm fuzzy search with similarity scoring for typo tolerance.
Results are ordered by relevance using trigram similarity scores.

Args:
    workspace_id: The workspace to search in. Required.
    title: Search query (case-insensitive). If empty or < 2 chars, returns recent documents.
    page: Zero-based page index. Default: 0.
    page_size: Number of items per page. Default: 20.
    session: Database session (injected).
    user: Current authenticated user (injected).

Returns:
    DocumentTitleSearchResponse: Lightweight list with has_more flag (no total count).

schema.title: Response List Messages Api V1 Threads  Thread Id  Messages Get

get.description:
Return the thread's paused HITL interrupts, if any.

The live approval card lives only in the frontend's in-memory stream
overlay, so a page refresh loses it while the LangGraph checkpoint stays
paused. The frontend calls this on thread load to re-render the card and
let the user resume or reject.

post.description:
Revert every reversible action emitted during ``chat_turn_id``.

Walks ``AgentActionLog`` rows for the turn in reverse ``created_at``
order so dependencies (e.g. ``mkdir`` -> ``write_file`` inside the new
folder) unwind in the right sequence. Each action is reverted in its
own SAVEPOINT so a single failure does not poison the batch.

Partial success is intentional and returned with HTTP 200. Callers
must inspect ``results[*].status`` to find rows that need attention.

from_message_id.title: From Message Id
from_message_id.description: A question or an answer of the turn to replace; an answer stands for its turn's question. History is replaced from that question on and the agent's state is rewound to just before it. Without it, the latest question. Legacy rows that predate migration 136 have ``turn_id=None``: the latest question is still rewound (by its message in the agent's state), an older one re-runs on the latest state, and ``revert_actions`` is ignored (no chat_turn_id available to walk).

revert_actions.title: Revert Actions
revert_actions.description: When true, every reversible action emitted at or after ``from_message_id`` is reverted before the regenerate stream begins. Per-action results are surfaced via the ``data-revert-results`` SSE event. Partial failures DO NOT abort the regeneration.

RegenerateRequest.title: RegenerateRequest
RegenerateRequest.description:
Request schema for regenerating an AI response.

This supports two operations:
1. Edit: Provide a new user_query to replace the question and regenerate
2. Reload: Leave user_query empty to ask the saved question again

The replaced turn is the one ``from_message_id`` belongs to, or the latest
one. Both operations re-run from the agent's state before that turn's
question (``flows/regenerate/rewind_point.py``), with the Tools menu pick
the question was asked with, and delete the question, its answer and every
later message once the re-run has moved the agent's state.

For edit, optional user_images (when not None) replaces the saved images
so the client can send the full user turn (text and/or images).

``revert_actions`` optionally reverts every reversible action emitted in
the replaced turns. The revert step is best-effort and runs BEFORE the
regenerate stream — partial failures are surfaced via SSE
``data-revert-results`` and do not abort the regeneration.

RevertTurnResponse.title: RevertTurnResponse
RevertTurnResponse.description:
Top-level response for ``POST /threads/{id}/revert-turn/{chat_turn_id}``.

``status`` is ``"ok"`` only when every reversible row succeeded. Any
``failed`` / ``not_reversible`` / ``permission_denied`` entry downgrades
it to ``"partial"``. Empty turns (no rows) return ``"ok"`` with an empty
``results`` list — callers should treat that as a no-op.

Counter invariant:
    ``total == reverted + already_reverted + not_reversible
              + permission_denied + failed + skipped``

Frontend toasts and the ``RevertTurnButton`` summary rely on this
invariant to display "X of Y reverted, Z could not be undone" without
silently dropping ``permission_denied`` or ``skipped`` rows.

UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate
UserUpdate.description:
What PATCH /users/me may change: the profile, nothing that signs in.

Not fastapi-users' ``BaseUserUpdate``: that takes ``email`` and
``password`` too, and changed them on a session alone, with no check of
the new address and no current password. A changed email is what single
sign-on and agent sign-in link a first-time identity to, so anyone with a
session (or someone who planted an account) could claim another person's
address. A password changes through "Forgot password?" (a mailed token);
an email only by the operator. Unknown fields are refused (422), so a
client that sends either learns it was not changed.
